description: Composite workflow-comparison schematic (process flow, not a data plot). A left column headed "Micrograph" shows a greyscale grain-boundary micrograph of "Pure iron" — equiaxed grains outlined in dark on a light matrix — which feeds into four stacked centre rows, one per extraction mode, and all rows converge on a right column headed "Final output" sub-labelled "Boundaries" (a binary grain-boundary network). (Mode 1) "Fully manual annotation" carries a full-width dark segmented time bar and three annotator icons. (Mode 2) "Rule-based (OTSU)" starts with a short four-segment bar, passes through an intermediate segmented grain image, and ends in "Manual correction" with one annotator icon and a medium-length teal bar. (Mode 3) "Learning-based (UNet)" is shown in grey with an intermediate image, "Manual correction" and a short grey bar. (Mode 4) "VLM-based (MatSAM)" is shown in red with an almost empty bar before and after "Manual correction". A legend at top right defines the segmented horizontal bar as "Time consumption". The figure's argument: the same grain-boundary output is reached by all four modes, but required annotation time (bar length) drops progressively from Mode 1 to Mode 4.
measured_quantities: relative time consumption of each extraction mode (segmented-bar length, arbitrary units; no numeric scale printed)

observations.observation: The input image of the workflow is a greyscale micrograph of equiaxed grains with dark boundaries, labelled "Pure iron" beneath the column heading "Micrograph".
The final output column is headed "Final output" and sub-labelled "Boundaries", and shows a black-on-white grain-boundary network of the same equiaxed grain structure.
A legend at the top right pairs the text "Time consumption" with a segmented horizontal bar symbol, which is used in every mode row as a relative time indicator.
Mode 1 is labelled "Fully manual annotation" and shows the longest (full-width) dark time-consuming bar together with three annotator icons.

Mode 2 is labelled "Rule-based (OTSU)"; it shows a short four-segment bar before an intermediate segmentation image and a medium-length teal bar at the "Manual correction" step with one annotator icon.
Mode 3 is labelled "Learning-based (UNet)" and is colour-coded grey, with an intermediate segmentation image and a short grey time bar at the "Manual correction" step (one annotator icon).
Mode 4 is labelled "VLM-based (MatSAM)" and is colour-coded red; both its pre- and post-correction time bars are almost empty, indicating the shortest human time of all four modes.
Modes 2, 3 and 4 each contain an intermediate segmentation image, whereas Mode 1 has no intermediate stage and is drawn as a single full-width annotation block.
No numeric time values are printed on any time-consumption bar; the comparison is purely by relative bar length.
The caption states the figure is a comparison of four modes of microstructure extraction.

The caption text accompanying the figure contains the fragments "Key structure (d) Overlay (b) NBS-3 (nickel-based superalloy) TCP phase", which describe content (an overlay panel and an NBS-3 superalloy TCP phase) that is not visible in this composite workflow figure — the caption appears to be mis-assembled or to mix text from another figure.
The extraction is presented as a single shared input micrograph feeding all four modes and a single shared "Boundaries" output, i.e. all four modes are claimed to reach the same segmentation product.

subfigures.description: Column headed "Micrograph" containing a greyscale optical/electron micrograph of equiaxed grains with dark boundaries, labelled "Pure iron"; this is the common input to all four modes.
Row titled "Mode 1": "Fully manual annotation" with a full-width dark segmented "Time consumption" bar and three annotator (person) icons; arrow leads directly to the final output.

Row titled "Mode 2": "Rule-based (OTSU)" with a short four-segment bar, an arrow to an intermediate segmentation image, then an arrow to "Manual correction" (one person icon) with a medium-length teal bar.
Row titled "Mode 3": "Learning-based (UNet)" in grey, with a short grey time bar, an intermediate segmentation image, then "Manual correction" (one person icon) with a short grey bar.

Row titled "Mode 4": "VLM-based (MatSAM)" in red, with a nearly empty red time bar, an intermediate segmentation image, then "Manual correction" (one person icon) with a nearly empty red bar — the least human time of the four.
Column headed "Final output" sub-labelled "Boundaries": black-and-white grain-boundary network extracted from the input micrograph; a single arrow from the input bracket serves all modes.

unreadable_items: Time-consumption bars carry no printed numeric values or units — only relative lengths are shown
Caption fragments "Key structure (d) Overlay (b) NBS-3 (nickel-based superalloy) TCP phase" refer to material/panels not present in this figure
Individual segment counts of the small grey and teal bars in Modes 2 and 3 are not reliably countable at the supplied resolution
